nodes.label: Vui Starter
nodes.author: VILIHA PTE. LTD.
nodes.rationale: One repo is both the published library and a reference admin app, so every component is demonstrated in a real screen instead of an isolated storybook.

nodes.label: Contributing to VUI Starter
nodes.rationale: CONTRIBUTING is the human-facing why (philosophy, PR flow); AGENTS.md is the machine-checkable what.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md (imports AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: A one-line @-import keeps AGENTS.md the single source of rules instead of duplicating them per agent tool.

nodes.label: Security policy (private advisories)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go through GitHub Security Advisories so the report stays confidential until a fix ships.

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct v2.1
nodes.norm_label: contributor covenant code of conduct v2.1

nodes.label: Enterprise Next.js & React Coding Standards
nodes.rationale: The human-facing rationale behind the terse rules in AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: VUI consumer agent guide (packages/ui/AGENT.md)
nodes.rationale: Ships inside the npm package so a downstream agent builds with the design system rather than reinventing it.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.template.md consumer pointer
nodes.rationale: Consumers copy a pointer file that @-imports AGENT.md, so the rules are never hand-copied and cannot drift.

nodes.label: @viliha/vui-core framework-free logic
nodes.rationale: Plain TypeScript with no UI framework so Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid or Node consumers get the logic without React.

nodes.label: @viliha/vui-theme design system as plain CSS
nodes.rationale: No JavaScript and no dependencies, so the tokens work in any framework or a hand-written HTML file with no build step.

nodes.label: pnpm workspace + Turborepo monorepo
nodes.rationale: apps/* and packages/* are the only workspace globs; the layout is intentional and must not gain a src/ root.

nodes.label: Supply-chain hardening (overrides, minimumReleaseAge, trustPolicy)
nodes.rationale: sharp and postcss are pinned forward past known CVEs; newly published versions wait 7 days, exotic sub-deps are blocked, and updates cannot downgrade security settings. The package.json overrides mirror exists because the pinned pnpm@9.0.0 reads only the mirror.

nodes.label: Configurable theme roadmap
nodes.author: Suman Bonakurthi
nodes.rationale: The theme ships finished and nothing about it is locked; preconfigured is a starting point, not a walled garden.

nodes.label: GitHub sponsor funding config
nodes.rationale: Sponsorship pays for maintenance, not for access; VUI is MIT and stays MIT.

nodes.label: apps/backoffice (admin app and docs site)
nodes.rationale: One app on :3000 both demonstrates the design system and hosts the docs at /docs, so there is no separate apps/docs package to keep in sync.

nodes.label: Free vs Pro split
nodes.rationale: Everything in the repo including the datatable is MIT; Pro is optional, additive, net-new work (premium blocks, Vue and Svelte datatables, priority support) that does not exist yet.

nodes.label: MIT permanence guarantee
nodes.rationale: Every version already published is MIT permanently, so nothing free today can move behind a paywall later. This is why a DCO sign-off is enough and no copyright assignment is needed.

nodes.label: Sponsorship keeps Vui free
nodes.rationale: An enterprise-grade admin theme is normally sold; sponsors fund the components, docs and demo that are given away instead.

nodes.label: Shipped as TypeScript source (no build step)
nodes.rationale: The consuming app's bundler compiles only what is imported, so the package is tree-shakeable and needs no dts step. The cost is that Next.js hosts must set transpilePackages.
nodes.norm_label: shipped as typescript source (no build step)

nodes.label: Install paths: Next.js, Vite, existing project, Turborepo
nodes.norm_label: install paths: next.js, vite, existing project, turborepo

nodes.label: Footer branding via NEXT_PUBLIC env vars
nodes.rationale: NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are read at build time and inlined into the static export, so they must be set where the deploy runs pnpm build.
nodes.norm_label: footer branding via next_public env vars

nodes.label: init scaffolder CLI
nodes.rationale: The package ships components; the shell and demo pages are scaffolded into the consumer's repo so they own and edit them. Upgrading the package deliberately does not touch scaffolded files, which is why some fixes need init --force.

nodes.label: VUI MCP server (seven tools)
nodes.rationale: list_guides, get_guide, list_components, get_component, list_pages, get_page, search_docs. The docs site ships inside the package as markdown so lookups work offline and match the installed version. A feature the MCP server cannot describe is not finished.

nodes.label: Auth contract, not an auth engine
nodes.rationale: Bundling NextAuth, Clerk or Supabase would force its SDK and backend on every consumer, so the package ships AuthProvider/useAuth plus types and the host writes one adapter. Swapping providers is one file, no screen changes.
nodes.norm_label: auth contract, not an auth engine

nodes.label: shadcn/ui components ported into the package
nodes.rationale: Restyled to VUI tokens and imported from @viliha/vui-ui/<name> so consumers stop maintaining a local components/ui copy and no shadcn token duplication is needed.
nodes.norm_label: shadcn/ui components ported into the package

nodes.label: Lazy-loaded picker options (loadOptions / resolveOption)
nodes.rationale: Fetching a whole reference catalog into a static options array on mount wastes requests when someone is only browsing. dependsOn handles cascades; resolveOption fetches the label for an already-set value.

nodes.label: RecordView fetcher (server-side read path)
nodes.rationale: RecordView owns fetching, data, rowCount, loading and abort of superseded requests, so a host does not hand-roll pagination. Preferred over manual mode for large server-backed lists.

nodes.label: RecordView cacheKey: the cache paints, the server decides
nodes.rationale: A cached page is only ever painted immediately; the request still goes out and its answer replaces what was shown, so the cache can never be the final answer (it could before 1.60). Cache the lookups, not the ledger: countries and tax codes for minutes, orders and stock never.
nodes.norm_label: recordview cachekey: the cache paints, the server decides

nodes.label: Trash and restore toggle
nodes.rationale: One table flips between live and soft-deleted rows instead of a separate deleted-records screen. RecordView is display-only here and never decides what deleted means; the host supplies trashed rows and persists onRestore.

nodes.label: BrandAsset image control
nodes.rationale: The package never touches host storage: onPick(file) uploads and returns a URL. The inline escape hatch stores base64 for demos only, because a 2 MB logo becomes a ~2.7 MB field value no ordinary column will take.

nodes.label: toast() module store
nodes.rationale: A module store rather than a context, so it can be called from any event handler or catch block with no provider. Toaster mounts once in the root layout.

nodes.label: FieldGrid + Field two-column standard
nodes.rationale: Label sized to max-content and aligned across rows so every control starts at the same x. The same standard as the filter panel and the auth screens, which is why a label is never stacked above its control.

nodes.label: Declarative filter panel
nodes.rationale: Mark fields filterable and handle onFilter; custom rows go through filterExtras composed with FilterField so the row layout is never hand-rolled.

nodes.label: TanStackChart (framework-neutral definitions)
nodes.rationale: Recharts has no Vue build, so charts that must exist in more than one framework use TanStack Charts, whose definitions render unchanged across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Angular. Optional peer dependency, so it costs nothing unless imported.

nodes.label: formSlots for custom content between fields
nodes.rationale: Slots are a prop on the form rather than entries in fields, because fields also drives the table, filter panel and import/export, so arbitrary markup in it would leak layout into all four.
nodes.norm_label: formslots for custom content between fields

nodes.label: behaviour config keys
nodes.rationale: rowClick, closeOnSave, flashMs, confirmDelete, confirmDiscardWhenDirty: what components do, as opposed to how they look. A key earns its place when a real screen needs it and the alternative is forking the component, never to restyle something the tokens own.

nodes.label: userConfigurable user-preference layer
nodes.rationale: Nothing is user-editable unless listed, which is the point: "the user prefers no row highlight" is a feature, "the user can move the Save button" is chaos. An unlisted key is ignored on write, so a stale stored value cannot leak back in.

nodes.label: onDataChange must return a promise
nodes.rationale: Returning nothing lets the reload race the POST and repaint the rows the server had before it, which is what makes a save look ignored. Returning the write promise makes the reload wait.

nodes.label: Opening a form is not a data change
nodes.rationale: RecordView keeps the unsaved draft out of the row list, so a poll, tab refocus or mutation elsewhere cannot pull the record out from under an open Add form. Only a save invalidates.
nodes.norm_label: opening a form is not a data change

nodes.label: Core philosophy priority order
nodes.rationale: Consistency over creativity, reuse over duplication, composition over configuration, simplicity over abstraction, then accessibility, performance, backward compatibility and enterprise UX. The goal is work that feels like it always belonged in VUI.

nodes.label: Delete first
nodes.rationale: Removing or reusing code almost always beats writing something new.

nodes.label: Extend before create
nodes.rationale: Add a variant or compose from existing parts; a brand-new component is the last resort.

nodes.label: Blueprint test for new components
nodes.rationale: A new component should be solid enough to be copied hundreds of times. If it feels too specific to the case in front of you, simplify it until it is not.

nodes.label: publish.mjs release wrapper
nodes.rationale: npmjs.com renders the README from the per-version readme field, which npm publish sends but pnpm, yarn-classic and bun do not, so the script always uploads via npm publish. It also strips workspace:* devDeps so the published manifest is spec-valid. A prepublishOnly guard blocks a bare publish.

nodes.label: DCO sign-off, no CLA
nodes.rationale: Contributed code stays in the MIT packages and is never moved into a commercial package, which is why a Developer Certificate of Origin is enough and copyright assignment is not.

nodes.label: Strict package boundaries
nodes.rationale: packages/ui holds primitives, tokens and theme.css with no application logic; apps/backoffice holds pages, business logic and the docs.

nodes.label: Accessibility is mandatory
nodes.rationale: Keyboard navigation, visible focus, screen readers, correct ARIA and WCAG AA contrast on every public component; jsx-a11y runs in CI at zero warnings.

nodes.label: Public APIs are contracts
nodes.rationale: Never rename props, change variants or remove exports; grow an API by extending it.

nodes.label: Recommended stack
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui plus @viliha/vui-ui, Recharts, TanStack Query, Zod, React Hook Form, Zustand when needed, Vitest + RTL + Playwright.

nodes.label: record-view.tsx single-module exception
nodes.rationale: Components aim for under 200 lines, but the datatable is one cohesive widget internally decomposed into RecordView, RecordDetailPanel, cell renderers and table-io helpers. A genuinely independent new concern gets its own file rather than growing this one.

nodes.label: utils.ts naming exception
nodes.rationale: utils.ts exists on purpose as the public @viliha/vui-ui/utils entry re-exporting cn; the general "avoid utils/helpers dumping grounds" rule still applies elsewhere.

nodes.label: Testing strategy
nodes.rationale: Start with pure logic (formatters, resolvers, io helpers) and critical widgets rather than chasing coverage.

nodes.label: Generated from packages/ui/src at publish time
nodes.rationale: @viliha/vui-core and @viliha/vui-theme are compiled from the same source the React components use, not hand-maintained, so the packages cannot drift. The build fails outright if a framework-free module picks up a framework import.
nodes.norm_label: generated from packages/ui/src at publish time

nodes.label: Runtime theming engine (THEME_FIELDS, themeToCssVars, applyTheme)
nodes.rationale: themeToCssVars derives a readable foreground from a brand colour, and parseTheme refuses values that could break out of a style attribute, so a theme loaded from an API cannot inject CSS.

nodes.label: Table import and export helpers
nodes.rationale: CSV and JSON round-trip, Excel is an HTML table saved as .xls, PDF is browser print. No dependencies, no worker, no 400 kB spreadsheet library.

nodes.label: 129 CSS design tokens in oklch
nodes.rationale: One --brand drives both light and dark through color-mix(), so a single saved value covers both modes and they cannot diverge.

nodes.label: Appearance tokens (data-sidebar, data-density, dir)
nodes.rationale: Three root attributes rearrange the shell without a re-render, and a host can set them server-side to avoid a flash on first paint.

nodes.label: Motion tokens
nodes.rationale: Duration and easing tokens drive every shipped animation so the feel is retuned without forking a keyframe, and motion is switched off in one line. That is a product choice, separate from prefers-reduced-motion, which is still honoured.

nodes.label: Icon chip opt-out
nodes.rationale: Radix icons get the bordered chip automatically because they render width="15"; .vui-icon opts another icon set in and --vui-icon-chip-border: none removes it app-wide.

nodes.label: .vui-chart token bridge
nodes.rationale: Maps the theme's chart tokens onto the six --ts-chart-* variables TanStack Charts reads, in pure CSS, so a chart follows light mode, dark mode and a per-tenant brand in any framework.

nodes.label: Vue components built on Reka UI
nodes.rationale: Reka owns the focus trap, scroll lock, positioning and aria wiring, the way Radix does on the React side, so only the surface classes are shared.
nodes.norm_label: vue components built on reka ui

nodes.label: Shared class strings, not copied
nodes.rationale: Both packages import the same class strings from @viliha/vui-core, and an SSR test compares the rendered Vue button against that same source, so the two cannot drift into looking almost alike.

nodes.label: Vue package gaps (v0)
nodes.rationale: Sheets, comboboxes, toasts, the command palette, the calendar, auth screens and the datatable are still React-only; issue requests decide the order.

nodes.label: Semver and Keep a Changelog policy
nodes.rationale: Patch for fixes, minor for backward-compatible features, major for breaking. A published version is immutable, so a fix ships as a new version.
nodes.norm_label: semver and keep a changelog policy

nodes.label: Upgrade guide 1.44 to 1.53
nodes.rationale: Everything from 1.50 on is additive; the behaviour changes before it all point the same way, which is to stop showing the user something meaningless (an Edit pencil on a read-only table, a raw id under a resolving label, a save that appears to revert).

nodes.label: Config resolution chain
nodes.rationale: package default, shipped preset, app config, user preferences, per-instance prop. Everything the preset does a host can do, because the preset uses the same API; if the shipped behaviour cannot be expressed in the config, the config surface is incomplete and that is a bug.

nodes.label: Slice 0: the config spine (shipped 1.50.0)
nodes.rationale: VuiConfig, vuiPreset, defineConfig, mergeConfig, useVuiConfig. Small, and everything else hangs off it.

nodes.label: Slice 1: form footer actions (shipped 1.50.0)
nodes.rationale: Highest value per day, zero risk, unblocks forms and settings at once: formActions, renderFooter, FormAction, FormActionContext.

nodes.label: Slice 2: form body composition (mostly shipped 1.52.0)
nodes.rationale: formSlots and fullWidth shipped; sections with tabs or accordions are still open.

nodes.label: Slice 3: page frames and the shell (open)
nodes.rationale: Turns five page types you copy from the docs into five you configure. Dashboard, settings and board are hand-built frames today, and copied markup is configurable only by editing it. The acceptance test is that the shipped preset drives the demo app and the demo still looks identical.
nodes.norm_label: slice 3: page frames and the shell (open)

nodes.label: Slice 4: behaviour (shipped 1.51.0)
nodes.rationale: The mechanism is small and the discipline is the work. Behaviour keys are also the first real customers for the user-preference layer, generalising what the top-bar toggles already do.

nodes.label: What stays closed on purpose
nodes.rationale: Tokens stay in theme.css with no per-component color or spacing props; fields stay described rather than hand-built because one array drives four surfaces; config is typed TypeScript with no visual builder and no JSON schema runtime.
